title: CPE 2.3 well-formed name (WFN) as a JSON object
description: DERIVED - not part of NISTIR 7695. A JSON shape the library defined so that test harnesses can exchange and validate WFNs. NISTIR 7695 section 5.1 says: "The WFN is a logical construct only. The WFN is not intended to be a data format, encoding, or any other kind of machine-readable representation for machine interchange and processing." so no specification defines this JSON form. Shape: an object whose keys are the eleven attribute names of section 5.2, written in lower case; an absent key is an unspecified attribute, whose value defaults to ANY (5.2 item 2). A value is either a string, holding the attribute-value string exactly as it appears between the double quotes of the wfn:[...] notation (backslash quoting included, so version "8\.0\.6001" is the JSON string "8\\.0\\.6001"), or an object {"logical": "ANY"} or {"logical": "NA"} for the logical values of 5.3.1. The patterns are compiled from figure-5-1-avstring.derived.abnf by ../examples/run-fixtures.derived.py, which fails if they drift.
$comment: Enforces: 5.2 item 1 (only the eleven attributes: propertyNames), 5.2 item 2 (each at most once: JSON object keys; duplicate keys in the JSON text are a parser matter and are not detected), 5.2 item 3 and 5.3 (each value is a logical value or a string), 5.3.1 (ANY, NA), 5.3.2 (string values: both Figure 5-1 and the prose of items 1 to 6, see $defs/string-value), 5.3.3.1 (part), 5.3.3.10 (language, RFC 5646 well-formedness only). Not enforced: 5.1 case-insensitive attribute names (this shape requires lower case), the SHOULD rules of 5.3.3 (valid-values lists, recommended content) and RFC 5646 registry validity.

logical.$comment: 5.3.1: the logical values ANY and NA.

avstring-figure-5-1.$comment: Figure 5-1 (5.3.2), rule avstring, compiled from figure-5-1-avstring.derived.abnf (PART 1). Accepts "*", "**", "?*" and "*?", which the prose forbids; rejects "\-?", which the prose allows.

avstring-prose.$comment: 5.3.2 items 1 to 6 under the library's readings P1 to P4, rule avstring-prose of figure-5-1-avstring.derived.abnf (PART 2).

string-value.$comment: A string value must satisfy both Figure 5-1 and the prose (the intersection, rule avstring-strict). Use only one of the two $defs above to apply one reading.

part-string.$comment: 5.3.3.1: "The part attribute SHALL have one of these three string values:" a, o, h (case-sensitive).

language-string.$comment: 5.3.3.10: "Values for this attribute SHALL be valid language tags as defined by [RFC5646]". The RFC 5646 section 2.1 Language-Tag production with every hyphen quoted ("en\-us"); RFC 5646 registry validity is not checked.
